the ACE I/D genotype is associated with LV function and that this association is modified by the presence of infarction and the extent of coronary disease.
the ACE gene polymorphism influences the left ventricular ejection fraction, but the influence is dependent on infarction status.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DD genotype, compared to the ID/II genotype is associated with lower LV ejection fraction in patients with a previous MI, and with a higher LV ejection fraction, in patients with no history of MI.
the ACE DD genotype is associated with better LV systolic function in noninfarction patients and with worse LV function in post-infarction patients, especially when the coronary arteries are patent.

the ACE I/D polymorphism is associated, in a population of Caucasian subjects with ischemic heart disease, with an improved LV function in noninfarction patients, whereas a reduced ejection fraction is observed in patients with a history of infarct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACE gene I/D polymorphism influences LV function in noninfarction patients and that the influence is more marked in patients with chronic coronary occlusion.

the ACE DD genotype, in comparison with the ACE ID or II genotype, is associated with lower left ventricular ejection fraction in patients with a history of myocardial infarct but with higher ejection fraction if no infarct is present.

the ACE I/D polymorphism is associated to a better LV systolic function in the absence of infarction but to a worse LV function in the presence of infarction, especially when coronary arteries are chronically occluded.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ACE I/D polymorphism influences LV ejection fraction in a complex way, which depends on the extent of the coronary artery disease and on whether or not an infarction had previously occurred.
ACE I/D gene variation may influence the response of the left ventricle to infarction and to chronic coronary occlusion.
the influence of the ACE gene I/D polymorphism on LV ejection fraction is modulated by the infarction history, the extent of coronary artery disease (CAD) and the patency of coronary arteries.
